title: Projects
subtitle: Code projects where I turn research, platform engineering, tooling, and product thinking into usable systems.
viewAllDescription: Browse the full project list, related repositories, and current status.

npu-computing-forecast.title: Ascend NPU Compute Forecasting Framework
npu-computing-forecast.summary: An experiment framework for teams running recommendation models on Ascend NPUs. It turns capacity planning from experience-based guessing into observable, reproducible, model-ready data.
points: Helps users estimate how model structure, batch size, and embedding scale affect NPU resource usage before occupying expensive hardware.
Turns one-off experiments into repeatable data collection workflows, reducing manual launch, note-taking, and log alignment errors.
Provides data foundations for scheduling, capacity planning, and model selection rather than only single-run benchmark numbers.
Uses configuration-driven experiment lifecycles with runtime snapshots so model and parameter combinations remain reproducible.
Collects NPU, CPU, cgroup, timestamp, and training metrics through DCMI, npu-smi, and host monitors.
Adapts WDL, DeepFM, DLRM, and DCN style models behind extensible model modules.
Connects hardware observation, experiment design, and model-ready feature extraction in one workflow.

crater.title: Crater Cloud-Native AI Platform
crater.summary: A Kubernetes-based AI training and inference platform from RAIDS Lab for labs and teams sharing GPU clusters. It combines compute allocation, development environments, workloads, monitoring, and documentation into one platform experience.
points: Lets researchers create Jupyter, Ray jobs, training tasks, and inference-related workloads without directly handling Kubernetes details.
Helps cluster administrators manage heterogeneous compute through UI, Helm charts, documentation, and monitoring.
Improves visibility and usability for shared GPU resources through scheduling, logs, monitoring, and platform abstractions.
Contributed to a real open-source platform through PRs spanning frontend, documentation, configuration, and platform engineering issues.
Works across Kubernetes, Helm, GPU scheduling, Jupyter, Ray, and vLLM-oriented platform workflows.
Maintains consistency between frontend, backend, documentation, deployment charts, and developer tooling.
Shows the ability to work inside a large collaborative codebase with deployment and regression concerns.

crater-cli.title: Crater CLI
crater-cli.summary: A Go CLI subproject in Crater for platform users, administrators, scripts, and AI agents. It turns platform operations, authentication, configuration, completion, and usage rules into a stable command-line interface.
points: Lets users complete login, configuration, and shell completion workflows in the terminal without depending on the web UI.
Gives scripts and CI stable JSON, exit codes, and error codes instead of forcing them to parse human text.
Gives AI agents clear operational boundaries so they can avoid unsafe actions against real accounts, credentials, and environments.
Organizes auth, config, completion, session, state, credential, and API modules around a Cobra command tree.
Defines structured errors, exit codes, pretty JSON output, and bilingual messages for users, scripts, and agents.
Adds unit tests, snapshot/golden tests, and sandboxing to avoid real credentials, network, and local state during regression checks.
Packages CLI usage guidance as distributable Skills so AI agents can call the platform safely.

undergraduate-thesis.title: Undergraduate Thesis: GPU Profiling Operator-Kernel Analysis
undergraduate-thesis.summary: Tools for analyzing ONNX Runtime GPU profiling traces and mapping model operators to low-level GPU kernels, helping researchers reduce manual guesswork in performance analysis.
points: Helps users locate expensive operators and related kernels inside large profiling traces instead of reading raw logs by hand.
Turns traces, statistics, and charts into reviewable evidence for thesis experiments and performance discussions.
Can be adapted to other model training or inference profiling scenarios because the value is in the reusable analysis workflow.
Extracts structured information from profiling traces and connects operator-level semantics with kernel-level performance data.
Uses Python analysis and visualization tooling to reduce manual GPU performance investigation work.
Bridges deep learning runtime behavior, GPU performance analysis, and research reporting.
Presents kernel_analyzer and kernel_data_plotter as one complete thesis project instead of isolated scripts.

model-requirements-evaluator.title: Inference Model Resource Evaluation Frontend
model-requirements-evaluator.summary: The frontend for an operating systems competition project. It helps users evaluate inference deployment cost by organizing models, GPUs, calculation workflows, and chart results into an operable web UI.
points: Lets users compare model and GPU configurations visually instead of only reading backend responses or static tables.
Visualizes latency, throughput, memory, and phase progress so users can understand trade-offs behind evaluation results.
Turns backend capability into an interactive product surface for competition demos and judging.
Built with Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, and Element Plus across model management, GPU management, and evaluation calculator views.
Uses ECharts and ECharts-GL for latency, throughput, memory, and phase progress visualization.
Keeps backend calls organized through model, GPU, evaluation, and chart service layers.
Turns algorithm/backend capability into a demonstrable and operable product surface for a competition setting.

tododag.title: ToDoDAG
tododag.summary: A DAG-based task management app for people overwhelmed by complex dependencies and long-running goals. It makes dependencies explicit so users can identify which tasks are actionable right now.
points: Helps users turn a stressful pile of tasks into Ready, Blocked, and Completed states so they know where to start.
Fits workflows such as thesis work, projects, job search, and coursework where tasks often depend on prerequisites.
Plans for local-first storage and private iCloud sync so personal planning data does not need a third-party server.
Centers the product model around Ready, Blocked, and Completed states, with cycle prevention and reliable persistence as core requirements.
Starts on macOS, with planned expansion to iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS using local-first storage and private iCloud sync.
Currently in an early planning/prototype stage with clear product boundaries and Apple-native UX constraints.
Shows product definition and data-structure thinking before implementation work begins.

personal-homepage.title: Personal Homepage and Content System
personal-homepage.summary: This site is also a long-running frontend project for HR, interviewers, open-source peers, and students. It organizes job-search material, open-source activity, content modules, and multilingual browsing as a maintainable static website.
points: Lets HR and interviewers understand my projects, direction, toolchain, and working style without searching across scattered repositories.
Lets visitors read in familiar languages while keeping sensitive resume files off the public site.
Turns personal presentation from a one-off page into a maintainable content system for projects, coursework, articles, and tools.
Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, and shadcn-style components, deployed to a GitHub Pages user site.
Supports light/dark themes, bilingual content, mobile-first layout, and reusable data for homepage highlights and module pages.
Keeps projects, workbench entries, directions, and future modules in structured content rather than hardcoded page components.
Uses .context task governance to preserve requirements, roadmap, active work, and archived decisions.
